executive_summary: An independent security review of the CDF TaskFlow codebase revealed multiple severe vulnerabilities across serverless edge functions, frontend components, and database access policies. The most critical finding is a SQL injection vulnerability in the task search function, allowing unauthenticated or low-privileged attackers to execute arbitrary database queries. Additional high-severity flaws include unauthenticated API endpoints using privileged service-role credentials, stored cross-site scripting in task comments, and mass assignment risks. Immediate remediation is required to implement parameterization, strict authentication checks, input sanitization, and proper row-level security controls before any production deployment.
overall_assessment: The application exhibits systemic security weaknesses typical of insecure prototype development. Edge functions rely heavily on privileged service-role keys without validating client session context or implementing authorization checks, effectively bypassing database row-level security. Furthermore, database queries utilize raw string interpolation instead of parameterized builders, and frontend components render unescaped user content. Addressing these issues requires refactoring serverless endpoints to verify user identity tokens, enforcing robust allowlists, sanitizing all rendered output, and correcting overly permissive database policies.
positive_observations: The project includes database migration files enforcing basic table constraints and role checks.
Project structure and TypeScript type definitions are clearly laid out.
Demo configurations and placeholder keys acknowledge security separation guidelines.
prioritized_actions: Refactor supabase/functions/search-tasks/index.ts to use parameterized queries instead of sql.unsafe() string interpolation.
Implement mandatory authentication token verification and authorization checks in supabase/functions/get-profile/index.ts and supabase/functions/update-task/index.ts.
Sanitize comment text before rendering or remove dangerouslySetInnerHTML in src/components/TaskComments.tsx.
Restrict overly permissive row-level security policies in supabase/migrations/002_access_policies.sql to enforce proper user data isolation.
Define explicit field allowlists for task updates to prevent mass assignment risks.
limitations: Static source-code review only: no code was executed, and no runtime or penetration testing was performed.
Deployment configuration, infrastructure, and third-party services outside the scanned files were not assessed.
Dependency versions were not checked against vulnerability databases (use npm audit / pip-audit alongside this tool).
Findings marked 'needs validation' depend on runtime context and should be confirmed by a developer.
No automated tool finds every vulnerability; absence of a finding is not proof of security.

findings.title: SQL Injection in Task Search Edge Function
findings.evidence:
const query = `
      SELECT id, title, description, status
      FROM public.tasks
      WHERE title ILIKE '%${searchTerm}%'
      ORDER BY created_at DESC
      LIMIT 25
    `;
findings.description: The search-tasks Edge Function interpolates untrusted query parameters directly into a raw SQL query string without parameterization, executing it via the `sql.unsafe()` driver method.
findings.impact: An attacker can execute arbitrary SQL queries against the database, leading to full database compromise, data exfiltration, or modification.
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries or the safe query builder provided by the database client rather than string interpolation and `sql.unsafe()`.
findings.secure_code:
const tasks = await sql`
      SELECT id, title, description, status
      FROM public.tasks
      WHERE title ILIKE ${'%' + searchTerm + '%'}
      ORDER BY created_at DESC
      LIMIT 25
    `;
findings.exploit_scenario: An attacker sends a request to `/functions/v1/search-tasks?q=%25' UNION SELECT id, title, description, status FROM public.profiles--` to extract sensitive profile records.
findings.review_note: The code clearly concatenates user input directly into an SQL string and passes it to sql.unsafe(), enabling arbitrary SQL injection.

findings.title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting via dangerouslySetInnerHTML
findings.description: Comment text is rendered directly as raw HTML using React's `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` sink without prior sanitization.
findings.impact: An attacker can post malicious JavaScript payloads in comments, leading to stored cross-site scripting when other users view the task comments.
findings.remediation: Avoid rendering raw HTML unless necessary. If rich text is required, sanitize the content using a robust library such as DOMPurify before passing it to `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, or render the text normally as a React node.
findings.exploit_scenario: An attacker posts a comment containing ``, which executes script code in the browser of any user opening the task details.
findings.review_note: Rendering user comments via dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization presents a direct Stored XSS vulnerability.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Privileged API Endpoint for Profile Retrieval
findings.description: The `get-profile` server function does not perform any authentication checks, session validation, or authorization checks to verify whether the caller is permitted to view the requested profile.
findings.impact: Any anonymous user can supply arbitrary user IDs to retrieve profile information, resulting in Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) and unauthorized data disclosure.
findings.remediation: Validate the caller's JWT/authorization header, verify that the authenticated user has permission to view the requested profile, and avoid using the service role key to bypass access controls.
findings.secure_code: // Validate auth header and caller identity before querying
findings.exploit_scenario: An attacker sends an unauthenticated GET request specifying another user's ID to fetch their private profile information.

related_locations.note: Supabase client initialized with service role key

findings.review_note: The Edge Function handles requests without checking any authentication or authorization token, while querying with the service role key.

findings.title: Mass Assignment Vulnerability in Update Task Edge Function
findings.evidence:
const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from("tasks")
      .update(changes)
      .eq("id", taskId)
      .select()
      .single();
findings.description: The `update-task` function takes the `changes` object directly from the request body and passes it to the Supabase update method without validation or an allowed field filter.
findings.impact: An attacker can modify restricted attributes or sensitive columns on records if Row Level Security is bypassed via the service role key.
findings.remediation: Define an explicit allowlist of modifiable fields and reject unallowed properties before updating the database.
findings.exploit_scenario: An attacker sends a crafted JSON payload containing administrative or ownership fields inside the `changes` object to take over tasks.

related_locations.note: Unvalidated request body fields used in database update

findings.review_note: Unvalidated request body objects passed directly to update operations allow mass assignment vulnerabilities.

findings.title: Permissive Row-Level Security Policies on Tables
findings.evidence:
CREATE POLICY "Users can view profiles"
ON public.profiles
FOR SELECT
TO authenticated
USING (true);
findings.description: Row-level security policies such as "Users can view profiles" and "Users can view tasks" use `USING (true)`, granting any authenticated user read access to all rows without filtering by ownership or association.
findings.impact: Authenticated users can read all records in the table, violating data isolation and privacy requirements.
findings.remediation: Restrict the `USING` clause to ensure users can only view records they own, are assigned to, or are authorized to access.
findings.secure_code:
CREATE POLICY "Users can view own profile"
ON public.profiles
FOR SELECT
TO authenticated
USING (id = auth.uid());
findings.exploit_scenario: A standard user queries the `profiles` or `tasks` table and receives records belonging to all other users.
findings.review_note: Using USING (true) on tables bypasses proper row-level access control, allowing any authenticated user to view all rows.

findings.title: Hardcoded Placeholder Secret in Frontend Code
findings.description: A credential-like key is hardcoded directly in client-side configuration source code. Although the value is explicitly marked as a placeholder, embedding secrets or keys in frontend bundles is an insecure pattern.
findings.impact: Hardcoded keys in frontend bundles are publicly readable by anyone inspecting the application code.
findings.remediation: Remove hardcoded keys from source code and load configuration values exclusively from runtime environment variables.
findings.exploit_scenario: An automated scanner or auditor flags the configuration file for embedded secret keys.
findings.assumptions: The value is a placeholder as indicated by 'NOT_REAL', but the pattern of embedding API keys in frontend code remains risky.
findings.review_note: Embedding configuration secrets in frontend code is an insecure pattern, even if marked as a placeholder.

static_signals.title: dangerouslySetInnerHTML renders raw HTML
static_signals.hint: React's escape hatch injects raw HTML. If the value can contain user-controlled content, this is stored/reflected XSS.

static_signals.title: Hardcoded secret-like value
static_signals.hint: A credential-like key is assigned a string literal in source code. Secrets in source end up in version control and, for frontend code, in the shipped JS bundle. The value looks like a placeholder/demo value; report the insecure *pattern* (secret embedded in source/client bundle) without claiming a leaked live credential.

static_signals.title: UPDATE policy on profiles does not protect column(s): role
static_signals.snippet: CREATE POLICY "Users can update own profile"
static_signals.hint: Row-level policies restrict *which rows* can be updated, not *which columns*. If the table has role/ownership columns and no column-level GRANT or trigger protects them, a user can update their own row to escalate privileges or reassign ownership.

static_signals.title: Policy "Users can view task comments" is not scoped to the current user
static_signals.snippet: CREATE POLICY "Users can view task comments"
static_signals.hint: The policy condition never references the requesting user (auth.uid()/JWT claims), so its result is the same for every user. Check whether it effectively grants all rows.
